reasoning: In the last 45 days, multiple high‑quality, Georgia‑specific general‑election polls of the 2026 U.S. Senate race (Jon Ossoff vs. Mike Collins) all show Ossoff with a mid‑single to low‑double‑digit lead. The AARP/Fabrizio Ward–Impact Research survey from July 13–16 has Ossoff +9 statewide, while summaries in AOL and Newsweek describe additional Fox News and Wick polls in late June–early July with Ossoff leads of +13 and +4, respectively; AOL notes the three recent polls together average roughly an Ossoff advantage of about 9 points. There is no new, state‑specific 2026 presidential general‑election polling in Georgia within the same window from major outlets, so the current discernible margin is **D+9** for the 2026 Georgia Senate race, with the presidential margin indeterminate based on available data.

sources.details: AARP’s Georgia poll of 1,060 likely voters shows Sen. Jon Ossoff at 52% and Rep. Mike Collins at 43% in the 2026 U.S. Senate race, an Ossoff lead of 9 points, with Collins ahead only among older voters.

sources.name: AARP (press release)

sources.details: Newsweek, summarizing a Wick poll of 1,175 Georgia voters, reports Ossoff leading Collins 47%–43%, a 4‑point Ossoff advantage in the Senate race.
